title: ernd turns AI bills into a corporate card rewards category
summary: ernd turns AI bills into a corporate card rewards category
body_markdown:
A startup buying AI services may be too small to negotiate much with its providers.[ernd](https://ernd.ai/) wants to aggregate that spending through a corporate credit card, offering rewards on AI bills alongside deals negotiated with infrastructure companies.


The Y Combinator Fall 2026 startup advertises 4% back on qualifying AI spending, 1.5% on other eligible purchases and no annual fee. The card is offered to US companies, with rewards belonging to the business rather than the employee who makes a purchase.


Founders Connor Dawson, Nikhil Ruia and Malcolm Wengel say the idea followed their own difficulty obtaining GPUs during the accelerator batch. As small buyers, they encountered unattractive pricing or unavailable capacity. Their response was to approach providers on behalf of a group of cardholders.


The card's rewards and its provider relationships are separate parts of that proposition. Paying an AI vendor can earn the advertised base reward without the vendor being an ernd partner. The company explicitly says OpenAI and Anthropic do not sponsor or endorse it.


[Watch ernd's original launch video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jy3HSLHD8uI) .


Its current[partner page](https://ernd.ai/partners) lists offers including 10% back on Wafer inference and twice the usage limits at Firecrawl. The offers vary by provider; Firecrawl spending, for example, earns the standard 1.5% card reward rather than the AI-category rate. Perks should not be read as one uniform package available across the entire stack.


The launch also describes priority GPU access and inference benefits as coming soon. Those plans should be distinguished from the specific partner offers currently listed. A rewards card cannot, by itself, establish that scarce computing capacity will be available when a customer needs it.


The business has a distribution angle for suppliers as well. Its partner page presents ernd as a way to reach startups choosing their technology providers, and discloses that Trace, Hopper and Agent 37 pay for listings. That gives cardholders another useful distinction: a recommended provider can also be a commercial partner.


Dawson previously worked on AI forecasting at Bridgewater's AIA Labs. Ruia's background includes data infrastructure at IMC Trading and payments work at Ripple. Wengel founded an investment fund and worked on financial AI agents. The founders also describe themselves as frequent credit-card rewards users.


According to ernd's YC profile, more than 30 startups requested the card in its first week and it signed eight partners. Requests are not issued cards or active spending accounts, so those figures indicate early interest rather than a disclosed transaction-volume milestone.


The[published terms](https://ernd.ai/terms) put issuance and account terms with the issuing bank, and say submitting a request does not guarantee approval. ernd determines which merchants qualify as AI vendors. Partner benefits can change, and some partner-funded rewards remain pending until the partner funds them.


The product's appeal will depend on the customer's actual vendor mix and the terms attached to those purchases. For ernd, the more ambitious question is whether many small AI buyers can become a group providers want to compete for, with the card serving as the connection between them.
